title: Undo puts the work order back with its old lead and in its old place
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Technicians {Technician-A} and {Technician-B} are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and Time Clock on.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682426 Ana and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C682426 Ben.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has three Approved work orders led by {Technician-A}, shown in that column in this order from the top: {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-3}. It also has an Approved work order {Work-order-4} with no lead technician. None has a shift booked on the Schedule. {Technician-B} is not the technician on any line of {Work-order-2}, and no line of {Work-order-4} has a technician.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682426 Undo Place, and {Work-order-1} to {Work-order-4} are S2-37441 to S2-37444.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Drag the card for {Work-order-2} from {Technician-A}'s column onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
  2. Click "Undo" on the message.
  3. Read the order of the cards in {Technician-A}'s column.
  4. Drag the card for {Work-order-4} from "Unassigned" onto {Technician-A}'s column and let go.
  5. Click "Undo" on the message.
  6. Click the card for {Work-order-2} to open the work order.
  7. Click ⋮ at the top right (next to "New Line"), then "Audit Log".
  8. Read the two newest "Lead tech changed" entries in the Work Order Log.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Work-order-2} moves to {Technician-B}'s column and the message "{Work-order-2} assigned to {Technician-B}" shows, with "Undo".
  • Step 2: the message closes, {Work-order-2} goes back to {Technician-A}'s column and the message "Assignment undone" shows, with no "Undo" button. No question about scheduled shifts appears.
  • Step 3: the cards read {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-3}, from the top, as before.
  • Step 4: {Work-order-4} moves into {Technician-A}'s column and the message "{Work-order-4} assigned to {Technician-A}" shows, with "Undo".
  • Step 5: the message closes, {Work-order-4} goes back to "Unassigned" and the message "Assignment undone" shows, with no "Undo" button.
  • Step 6: the work order page opens and Lead Technician reads {Technician-A}.
  • Step 7: the Work Order Log opens.
  • Step 8: the newest entry is the Undo, {Technician-B} → {Technician-A}, and the one before it is {Technician-A} → {Technician-B}. Both show your user and the time.

Known problem (SV-11524, open; seen on staging by the designer on 19 Oct 2026): the message reads "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") and has no Undo button. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 19 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician from the board or grouped table); tickets SV-11522 (Tech View) and SV-11524 (Board View)

  • S4-R32: “Undo puts the work order back exactly as it was before the change: the previous lead technician (or Unassigned), its previous place in that technician’s order, and any shifts the change cleared (removed shifts come back as they were; a shift that was ended at the moment of the change gets its original end time back). Undo is itself a lead change: it records its own audit entry (S4-R9), follows the Invoiced or Paid rule (S4-N2), and shows no shift-clearing prompt. After Undo the design’s toast reads “Assignment undone”, with no Undo button on it. If Undo cannot be saved, nothing changes and the alert “Couldn’t undo the change. Please try again.” shows.”
  • S4-R9: “Every lead-change path records one audit entry with the previous lead, new lead, logged-in actor, and time.”

Not yet checked against a build.
